# rMBP ledger — every finding, ticked once

> Arch ledger for the 2012 rMBP (x86_64) track. Cross-arch and shared-seam items live in
> `docs/dev/LEDGER.md` (ids `S<n>`, `P<n>`); rows below cross-reference it by id.

> Rule (`docs/dev/LAWS.md` §Ledgers, Peter 2026-09-05): **an arc that fixes, flies, or drops a ledger
> item ticks it here in the same commit.** Every audit, inventory, or capture review folds its findings
> into this table the turn it lands. Before spawning any audit, brief it with this file: report only
> what is NEW or CHANGED. A finding re-derived because it was not here is the waste.

Columns: `owner` = the lane whose file changes (orin · pi · rmbp · shared-gate); `flies-on` = the bench that scores it.
Status enum (GATE-LEDGER): **open** · **fixed-unflown** · **flown** · **landed** · **dropped** — free text after " — ".

P7 (SECSTA2) adds the SECOND W1C clear, taken after the last bus walk of the boot, so P6's `d_secsta`/`d_lnksta` at the first stall are deltas against the end of enumeration; its `relatch=` field measures which RW1C bits enumeration itself sets — the premise the "`secsta=2000` is residue" reading rests on and which nothing had ever measured. A third finding landed with it, again about evidence: the residual P6 recorded named the wrong walk — `ehci::init` (`arch/x86_64/pci.rs:838`) runs BEFORE the at-arm clear (`arch/x86_64/pci.rs:1016`), so the EHCI enumeration was never the leak **P7 IS NOW COMPLETE: DEVSTA (2026-09-15, `exec-rmbp-smallfix4`, parent `1c7c1733` — re-derive the sha at the land) closed the leftover SECSTA2 named in its own text** ("closing it is two lines here, read `cap + 0x0A`, clear `DEVSTA_W1C`, store it — left to the seat rather than taken silently"). Device Status is now read, RW1C-cleared on the same CF8 write path and re-baselined with its two neighbours, so the `wedge-sample` line's `d_lnksta`/`d_secsta`/`d_devsta` **all** delta against the end of enumeration instead of two against one window and the third against `pci::init`'s Kepler dispatch; the post-enum line carries `devsta=<before>-><after>` and `relatch=… devsta:<bits>`. The VALUE is unchanged expectation (`devsta=0000` on every capture there has ever been); what is fixed is a READING HAZARD — three deltas printed on one line read as one measurement, and one of them was not. A `d_devsta=0004` (Unsupported Request Detected, the likeliest bit for a read of a wedged BAR) could have been latched by any of the three post-at-arm enumeration walks with nothing on the wire to say so. Three scoring rows for `relatch=devsta:` are added to PCIE-RP-RECOVERY.md §11.3, so the flight scores it rather than reading it. **CORRECTION 2026-09-16 (STEALMS, branch `exec-rmbp-stealms`, parent `5ebe29f4`; tip sha at the fold — a commit cannot name its own hash): the sentence above, "no `REHOMED`, no `DEAD c<n>` on either boot", is FALSE on the capture this row cites.** Measured: `LC_ALL=C grep -a -c -F 'REHOMED the render role' capture/rmbp12-flight8/ttyUSB0.log` = 7 and `LC_ALL=C grep -a -c -F 'GATE STOLEN' capture/rmbp12-flight8/ttyUSB0.log` = 7 (control `LC_ALL=C grep -a -c -F 'ZZZNOTPRESENTZZZ'` = 0; four on flight 8, three on flight 9), every steal `after 4016-4303ms`, `revenants=0` throughout: both machines survived by LOSING a core per stall, not by not stalling — flight 8 lost c1, c2, c3, c4 in 63 s and ran render on c5. In the same commit the steal bound `COMP_GATE_STEAL_MS` (`video/wm.rs:9496`) is lowered 4_000 -> 1_500 ms (5x the 302 ms record honest pass, 1.5x `COMP_PASS_OVERDUE_MS`; B116): each freeze becomes ~1.5 s instead of ~4 s, the core is still lost, W5 stays the repair; the next stall must print `GATE STOLEN … after 15xx ms`, never `4xxx`. **FALSIFIED AND FIXED 2026-09-17 (W5SPIN, branch `exec-rmbp-w5spin`, parent `4638014e`; the tip sha at the fold, a commit cannot name itself): STEALMS's lowered bound worked — flight 10 printed `after 1528ms`, `after 1750ms`, `after 1768ms`, never `4xxx` — and I2's NMI then refuted the reading the whole row rests on. All three dead cores answered the NMI (`:: W5: nmi core=c1/c2/c3 taken=y … in_blit=n cs=0x8 icr=ok ::` at 665828 / 668402 / 841827 ms), so they were EXECUTING, not parked on a non-retiring store; no rip was inside `memcpy=0x79454510..0x7945453f`. At load offset `0x7915a000` the rips `0x79253da2` / `0x79253da6` / `0x79253da6` resolve on the flown ELF to `video::wm::present_banded + 0x462` and `+ 0x466` — two instructions of ONE unbounded test-and-test-and-set spin, `pace_shadow_refresh`'s `PACE_SHADOW[slot].lock()` (`wm.rs:2119`) inlined. The three differing `at=` phases (`pw-strip` phase 42 win 10, `span-flush` phase 33 win 7, `pw-exit` phase 49 win 9; `blit_inflight` 0, 1, 0) are the same fault: `COMP_PASS_PHASE`/`WIN`/`ROW` are gauges stamped by the gate holder (`wm.rs:10130`) and name where the holder's PASS last stamped, not where the core is. So this row's `a core dies mid-blit` is wrong: the core waits mid-PRESENT for a shadow lock its own suspended pass pins, the 1.5 s steal declares it dead, nothing ever resumes the pass, the `MutexGuard` is orphaned and the next presenter of that window dies the same way — which is exactly the c1 to c2 to c3 cascade on the wire. FIXED in the same commit: the refresh-side acquire is bounded (one try-lock, then a 500 us budget), gives up with `:: [wcser] PRESENT-BANDED SPIN site=<n> waited_us=<n> on=shadow<n> -> GAVE-UP ::`, clears the window's shadow-validity bit so it falls back to the documented live-read path, and RETURNS — so the core is never the holder that had not moved and the steal is never reached. Status of the ROW itself is unchanged where it is about hardware: W4 stays exonerated, W2 confirmed, and why the GK107 sits in the standing latch (`pri_fault=0x80300001`, `bar1_fault=0x22010860/0x8482d000/0x00000002/0x00221500`, identical at all three stalls) is still open as W5's hardware half. What the capture ALSO carries is 3697 `:: [wcser] PRESENT-BANDED SPIN` lines — 2008 at site=2 (1695 `-> GAVE-UP` + 313 `-> RELEASED`) and 1689 at site=1 (all `-> RELEASED`, none a give-up) — and every one of the 1695 `-> GAVE-UP` arms reads `waited_us=500` — the WHOLE budget, never a near miss — on shadows 6..12 only (386/183/302/450/146/127/101, summing to the total; the seven vugs, never the console or the shell), each immediately followed by its `site=1 waited_us=0 -> RELEASED` twin, i.e. the lock was FREE microseconds later. So the give-up is not contention luck: `composite_inner`'s `_shadow_pin` is held for the WHOLE per-window iteration, and `[comp2] pass_us=139751 max_us=250007 compose_us=60954 present_us=32066 util_pct=97 rate=6.9/s` makes that ~14 ms per window against a 500 us budget — 28x. Only `compose_us` reads a shadow byte; `present_us` is the BAR1 blit and the ~46.5 ms/pass residual is `beam::hold` spinning (`[wc-h] win=8 beamwaits=4336` with `beamwait_us` summing to 10 766 899, a 2.48 ms mean, and `win=2 beammaxwait_us=62007`), so the BEAM WAIT ALONE exceeds the presenter's entire budget by 5x before a single BAR1 byte moves. THE BOUND WAS NEVER TOO SMALL; THE CRITICAL SECTION WAS TOO WIDE, which is what `pace_shadow_acquire`'s own header described (`the pass pins the shadow across draw_window + WC-G/WC-D + the staged span-flush ... which is milliseconds at best`) and then bounded the other side of. FIXED in VUGPERF by giving the pass its own buffer (`PACE_MIRROR`, B135): the shadow lock is now held for one `surf_len` memcpy and released inside `pace_shadow_source`. RBTDRAIN on `exec-rmbp-rbtdrain` (the sha is the commit carrying this row; a self-referencing sha cannot be written into its own commit, so the seat folds it at the land): the design this row asked for, built. `xhci::ftdi_flush_sync(budget_cycles) -> (bytes, transfers, exhausted)` pumps `drain_ftdi` until the FTDI mirror ring is empty or the budget is spent, takes the controller with `claim()` (the WEDGE-8 loan — answers `Busy`, never waits: the LOCKFIX path this row names) and retries only INSIDE the budget, so a wedged pass costs the reboot its budget and never the machine. Two call sites and neither is redundant: `power.rs` calls it after `power_drain` on BOTH x86 verbs and then writes `[pwrreboot] ftdi flushed bytes=… transfers=… exhausted=0 (or 1)` into the ring, and `acpi_power::reboot`'s FIRST statement (line-neutral fold on the signature, as S5DRAIN's is on `poweroff`'s) is the same call — which is what carries that line to the cable, and is also the last point before `interrupts::disable()` at which the TX pump's `hlt()` can still wake. UNGATED: transport correctness, the same standing `power_drain` and `s5_ring_flush` have; NO new knob. `drain_ftdi` gained a bool return (true = nothing left to push, false = PTBURST slice yield) for this and nothing else. QEMU-green, UNFLOWN on metal (no rMBP boot since). BOTH x86 power ports carry the fold: `acpi_power::poweroff`'s signature line is `s5_ring_flush(); ftdi_flush_sync(…)` in that order (S5DRAIN's 'first statement' property unmoved), so `video/crystal.rs`'s Shut Down and `video/instgui.rs`, which call `poweroff` DIRECTLY, reach the cable too. ⚠ RESIDUAL, found by this fixture and NOT closed here: `[pwrreboot] ring drained lines=N bytes=M` is on serial.log and NOT on the cable — `serial_ring::power_drain` writes the drained lines AND its tally through `arch::serial::raw_write_str`, the 16550 alone, never through `_print`, so on this laptop PWRDRAIN empties the staging ring into a port that is not there and a line DEFERRED under contention is consumed before any FTDI flush can see it. What RBTDRAIN carries is everything `_print` reached the mirror ring with. (2) THE DOOR: arming the knob was not enough — x86 had no route to `quarry::open()` at all, because the x86 click router calls `dock::press_at` directly and never reached the `strip::press_route`->`quarry::service()` pair the aarch64 router uses, so the tile latched `request_open()` and no pass on the arch ever drained it. **CLOSED by QUARRYX86-2**, one `#[cfg(feature = "quarry")] crate::video::quarry::service();` folded onto `arch/x86_64/syscall.rs:7497`'s consumed-press arm (line-neutral; the `quarry` gate, not `desktop_firmware`, because `video/mod.rs:685` admits the module on x86 under `wc`). See PARITY.md §9. (3) THE CONTENT, found on flight 10 and the third distinct defect behind the same sentence: Quarry OPENS on x86 now, and every click INSIDE the opened window was consumed undelivered — `[clickroute] press at (920,604) win=5 owner=0xffffff03 was=0 -> consume deliver=0`, three times, which is the router's kernel-furniture arm saying the point resolved to a kernel-owned row with no input ring and no arm that names Quarry. **fixed-unflown by QUARRYCLICK**: one statement folded onto the `}` that closes the dock arm in `wc_click_route_at`, calling a `wc_quarry_press` helper appended at `arch/x86_64/syscall.rs`'s tail, which reaches the SAME shared entry aarch64 reaches (`video/quarry/live.rs::press_route`, exported under `feature = "quarry"` for both arches with no `target_arch` on it and documented as taking PANEL coordinates, so nothing had to be un-gated and no coordinate conversion is done). Position is the aarch64 twin's and is a contract: after the furniture bands, ahead of WMDIRECT's chrome arm, so Quarry keeps its own close disc while chrome and the minimise/zoom discs still fall through and it stays draggable. Wire after: `-> quarry` where flight 10 read `-> consume`, plus a new `[quarry] press at (sx,sy) row=N kind=… -> cd / select / launch / miss` line on both arches (an in-window press printed nothing before this arc). (5) THE OPEN GESTURE, Peter on flight 11: *"quarry rows open fine, but could not open a file"* — and the capture says the gesture was never MADE, which the old wire could not have told anyone. flight 11's serial capture (seat-local, read with `awk index()`; the executor's read-only slice is named in the arc's commit): the two presses on the file row are `[ 844506ms] press at (399,427) row=15 kind=file -> select` and `[ 851023ms] press at (389,425) row=15 kind=file -> select`, **6517 ms apart**, with `[ 846253ms] press at (18,527) row=1 kind=dir -> select` — a TREE press — between them; `is_double` tests the pane as well as the row, so that press re-stamped `click_pane = Pane::Tree` and broke the pair on a second, independent ground. No window width would have opened that file. THREE REPAIRS, **fixed-unflown by QUARRYOPEN**. (a) THE WIRE NAMED NOTHING: `kind=file -> select` was one line for `VUG.ELF`, for a screenshot and for `CONFIG.TXT`, and a double-press on an UNOPENABLE file printed `-> miss` (the second press changes no selection, no focus and no cwd, so the model diff read "nothing happened" for a gesture the window heard and refused). The press line now carries the decision — `-> open kind=… handler=…` (kind is one of png, elf, bin, text, unknown; handler is facet or launch) and `-> select (no handler for .TXT)` — `[quarry] open UNHANDLED`'s sentence *"no opener exists in this tree"* was rewritten because FACET (`3c6e406a`) made it false, and `<Enter>` (which has opened the selected row since M2 and said only `key=0x0d focus=1 took=1`) now prints `[quarry] enter row=N kind=… -> …` from the SAME `act_tail` over the same `Act`, so the pointer and the keyboard cannot describe one decision two ways. (b) THE WINDOW IS MEASURED ON THE DRAIN CLOCK, not on the report: `press_route(x, y)` takes two coordinates on both arches, so the only `arch::ms()` the gesture can reach is the one `content_press` takes when the click router runs it. Flight 11 measured that lag by pairing each `:: PTR: [1] press … (down edge)` with the `[quarry] press` it produced — **264 / 200 / 300 ms**, against `[ptrinstall] lag_max_ms=678` (744 later in the same flight) — so `is_double` tests `Δreport + (lag₂ − lag₁)` and 400 ms dropped a real ~180 ms double-press whenever two drains differed by >~220 ms. `DOUBLE_CLICK_MS` 400 -> **500** (the gesture's ~180 ms plus the measured ~100 ms of drain spread; deliberately short of `lag_max_ms`, because Quarry's single press SELECTS and a 678 ms window makes a slow re-select an accidental launch). The real repair is a report stamp threaded through the two router files — one is another lane's, one is the knob-off `kernel8.img`'s byte-identity file — and it is written down as `quarry.md` §7.1 rather than half-built here. (c) THE GESTURE HAD NO FIXTURE ON x86 AT ALL: the double-press was driven only by leg 11 of `selftest_result`, which hangs off `quarry::selftest`, which the x86 battery never calls (x86 reaches `crystal::selftest` -> `door_selftest`). New `open_selftest` (`:: QUARRYOPEN: … ::`) is chained from BOTH arms with its own `DONE` latch and drives `press_and_witness` — the function `press_route` itself calls, one lock deeper — so the battery puts REAL `[quarry] press at …` lines on the wire, readable with the same `awk index($0,"[quarry]")` a flight capture is read with. Disk-free, stops at the `Act` (the handler's own witness is QUARRYLAUNCH's, in the same battery). | B131 | **THE WIFI3 UPLOAD GATE REFUSED ON A TERM ITS OWN SPEC SEQUENCE CLEARS THREE WRITES LATER, AND THE "METAL EVIDENCE" THE LADDER CITED FOR SHM ACCESS HAD NEVER EXECUTED.** Flight 11 (2026-09-22), the first armed `UNAOS_WIFI3=1` boot, reached the upload rung and stopped at its third precondition: `:: wifi2: upload REFUSED reason=macctl-shape macctl=0xc0020403 shm-enabled=0 want=1 big-endian=0 want=0 … NOTHING has been written ::`, `upload NOT ATTEMPTED uploaded-bytes=0(audited) wrote-core-regs=0(audited)`, `:: wifi4: end ok=0 stage=gate ::`. Everything above it behaved (`WALK-OK`, `d11 FOUND id=0x812 rev=29` four MATCHes, `reachability=SATISFIED(no-write)`, `set-validation verdict=VALID`) and nothing destructive happened. **THE TERM WAS WRONG, AND THE REFUTATION NEEDED NO METAL — IT IS INTERNAL TO THE SEQUENCE THE SAME FUNCTION PERFORMS SIXTY LINES LOWER.** `[SPEC-V3 ChipInit]` step 1 = "Write 0x404 to MMIO offset 0x120" (fact 4.1, ABSOLUTE), step 2 = "Microcode and PCM upload", step 4 = "Write 0x20402 to MMIO offset 0x120". Decoded against `[SPEC-V4 802.11/Registers]` (fact 2): `0x404` = IHR Region Enabled (0x400) + PSM Jump 0 (0x4); `0x20402` = Infra (0x20000) + IHR Region Enabled + PSM Run (0x2). **`SHM Enabled` (0x100) is CLEAR in BOTH words that bracket the upload**, so the spec streams the microcode through the SHM window with the bit clear BY CONSTRUCTION, and `[SPEC-V3 MicrocodeUpload]` imposes no MACCTL precondition at all — only "control word 0x03000000, 32 bits at a time". The gate was refusing its own spec: had the bit arrived set, the rung would have passed and then **cleared it itself** at step 1. **THE CONSTANT WAS NEVER THE PROBLEM (question (b), answered):** `[SPEC-V4 802.11/Registers]`'s MAC Control table gives 0x1 MAC Enabled, 0x2 PSM Run, 0x4 PSM Jump 0, **0x100 SHM Enabled**, 0x200 SHM Upper, 0x400 IHR Region Enabled, 0x10000 Big Endian Mode — fact 2's transcription exactly — and revision-qualifies only 0x100000/0x200000 ("Used only for 802.11 core revisions 11 and 12"), so **0x100 carries no rev-29 caveat**. What was wrong was the INFERENCE from the name, not the name or the value. **AND THE SECOND FINDING, which is the one that let the first stand unchallenged: §S4-W5 fact 1 called `0x0001` "the value S4a already proved on metal" and fact 5 called it "S4a's metal-proven path" — BOTH FALSE.** §S4a's own Result block still reads `UCODEREV=<unflown> … no boot has executed this code`; `drivers/bcma.rs`'s probe sits behind `bcmaS1`; **flight 11's capture contains ZERO `wifi-s4a:` lines** because the arc-2 rewrite in `src/wifi/` never calls it. **No boot of this machine had ever read a shared-memory word**, yet two sentences had promoted a second transcription of a spec table into a measurement, and a destructive rung's precondition inherited that confidence. Both sentences corrected in place; the same false claim in `bringup.rs`'s `SHM_ROUTE_SHARED` doc comment corrected with them. **THE FIX (question (c), decided):** the `SHM_ENABLED` term is REMOVED from the gate and REPORTED on the wire instead, on the authority of ChipInit steps 1/2/4; `BE` stays gated **and alone** (the be32-file-to-u32-port framing really is wrong by a swap under Big Endian Mode, and nothing in the spec sequence sets or clears it for us); `SHM_UPPER` is reported and gated on nothing (routing 0x0300 is the microcode bank, not a shared-memory index — the upper-bank bit bears only on the fact-5 handshake, which has its own ladder). Refusal renamed `macctl-shape` → **`macctl-big-endian`**: a reason token naming a "shape" when one term is checked is the same overreach in miniature. **THE IN-BOOT FALSIFIER, ahead of the gate:** a new READ-ONLY `:: wifi2: shm-probe routing=0x0001(Shared Memory, [SPEC-V3 SHM] fact 1's table) ctl-wrote=0x00010000 ctl-readback=… shared[+0x00]=… macctl=… shm-enabled=… shm-upper=… big-endian=… window-answers=YES or NO(all-ones …) or NO(all-zero …) ::` selects shared routing 0x0001 at byte offset 0 and reads one 16-bit word through `SHM_DATA`. It writes **`SHM_CONTROL` only** — the read path's address-window selector — so no data-port write, no MACCTL write, no reset, the resident PSM untouched: §S4a's safety argument applied to §S4a's own access, executed for the FIRST time. `window-answers=YES` beside `shm-enabled=0` is direct metal proof that host SHM access does not require the bit; a `NO` leaves the spec argument standing alone, and the all-zero leg deliberately does NOT separate "window off" from "nothing published here". Nothing downstream gates on it: evidence, not permission. **AUDIT INTEGRITY, the trap this arc had to avoid recreating:** the probe is a real d11 core-register write, so it is counted at the site and `upload_not_attempted`'s note plus `end_line`'s `CORE_REGS_NOTE` are amended to name it — **the count discriminates: 0 = the rung returned before the probe (preconditions a/b), 1 = the probe alone and no destructive write was made.** An audited zero that the same call frame violates is exactly the fault §S4a's L0 write-up was written to make impossible, and arming a write without amending those notes would have reproduced it. | rmbp | rmbp | fixed-unflown — WIFISHM (branch `exec-rmbp-wifishm`, parent `b9edcfa1`). The destructive step is UNCHANGED and still fully gated: prologue guard (fact 7's IOCTL shape), container re-verify, and now BE alone — every term the gate checks is still printed on the refusal line. Clean room: every constant carries its `[SPEC-V3 …]`/`[SPEC-V4 …]` tag; the two spec wikis named in §S4-W5 were the only sources read; no driver source. | B133 | **THE CTRLBIND RESTORE UNWOUND THE CHANNEL IN THE BRINGUP'S ORDER, AND A BRINGUP'S ORDER IS EXACTLY WRONG FOR ITS OWN UNDOING — flight 11 printed `verdict=DIRTY` and the read-back is the only reason anyone knows.** KF9b captures PFIFO_CHAN[1] +0x00/+0x04 before the audit and puts them back after it. Flight 11: `ctrlbind begin chan00=0x00000000 chan04=0x00000000`, twelve binds, then `chan-restored 00=0x00000000(want 0x00000000) 04=0x00000001(want 0x00000000) verdict=DIRTY`. **WHICH WRITE SET BIT 0: none of ours.** `try_bind_and_witness` writes `+0x00=0`, `+0x04=0x00000400`, the VALID bind word (`0xC0000000` ored with `inst>>12`) into `+0x00` — bit 0 appears in no operand — and `+0x04` then reads `0x11000001` on all twelve rollups and on `init`'s thirteenth. So the chip sets bit 0 in response to the VALID bind word going into `+0x00`; it is CHANNEL STATE, not our residue. **WHY THE RESTORE MISSED IT, and the discriminator is in the same word:** the restore's `+0x04=0` DID clear `0x11000000` and did NOT clear bit 0. Same write, same cycle, two outcomes — so this is not "the write was ignored" but "the chip was holding one bit", and it was holding it because the write landed while the channel was STILL BOUND: the restore wrote `+0x04` first and released `+0x00` second, on the seam comment's reasoning that "the word carrying VALID is the last one written here exactly as it is in the bringup". That rule is a BIND's rule. `+0x00`'s entry value is `0x00000000` and carries no VALID at all, so writing it last released the channel AFTER the status word had already been put back against a live channel, and re-reading found the bit. **THE FIX is the order, not a new register or a new write:** release `+0x00` FIRST, put `+0x04` back LAST, read both. The line now carries `order=00-then-04` and a verdict that NAMES its residue — `clean` / `DIRTY-chanstate` (`+0x04` off in bit 0 alone) / `DIRTY` — because a restore that reports one undifferentiated DIRTY cannot tell "we left the channel armed" from "the chip holds a bit no write clears", and those want opposite next moves. **WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLAIM.** It does not claim the next boot prints `clean`. If bit 0 survives a release as well, `DIRTY-chanstate` is the finding — a latch no write clears — and that is a reading the old line could not have produced. **The brief's alternative (restore to `init`'s post-bind value because clearing an ENABLE on a live channel is something `init` would never do) DOES NOT APPLY and is recorded here so nobody re-proposes it:** the entry value of `+0x00` is `0x00000000`, so after this restore the channel is NOT live — VALID is down — and there is no live-channel ENABLE to preserve. Restoring to `0x11000001` would also have made the verdict a success echo, since that is the value the seam's own last bind leaves and no write could fail to "restore" it. **LESSON, one line: a capture/restore pair around a device probe must unwind in the order that RELEASES first, and its read-back must name which word and which bit disagreed, or the restore is a ritual.** | rmbp | rmbp | fixed-unflown — KF9CLOSE on branch `exec-rmbp-kf9close`, parent `b9edcfa1`. **The change is the ORDER of two existing `mmio_write`s plus the verdict arms; no register is touched that KF9b did not already touch, and no write is added or removed.** LINE-NEUTRAL by construction: the sixteen lines of the restore block were replaced by sixteen lines, so kepler.rs's total line count is unchanged and no `panic::Location` below it moved (B94's trap). Gates: `cd unaos && ./arroyo check` exit 0 both arches; `./arroyo knoboff nvidia-kepler-ctrlbind b9edcfa1` and `./arroyo knoboff nvidia-kepler-ctrladdr b9edcfa1` both exit 0; the QEMU suite exit 0 and COMPLETE with the Kepler path declining (`:: kepler: no-device ::`), plus an artifact grep proving `:: kepler: ctrlbind chan-restored` is IN the armed image, and an artifact-level MUTATION (the `+0x04` restore statement deleted) proving the image moves when it goes — which is all QEMU can buy here, having no Kepler. OWED: one boot, to print `verdict=clean` or `verdict=DIRTY-chanstate` and settle which | `unaos/crates/kernel/src/drivers/gpu/kepler.rs` (the KF9b restore block, `kepler.rs` ≈:1792); the fourteen `ctrlbind` rollups of flight 11, 2026-09-22, quoted verbatim in register §2's KF9b row (the raw capture is the seat's and is not yet folded under `docs/dev/evidence/`); `docs/dev/OS/08_VIDEO/SHUTOUT-REGISTER.md` §2 KF9 + KF9b, §7 KF9, §9; `docs/dev/OS/rmbp-queue.md` `SHUTRESTORE-CTRLADDR-BRINGUP` | — |
| B134 | **THE POINTER INSTALL WAITS ON THE COMPOSITOR IN ITS FIRST STATEMENT, and "sticky" is a FOLDED RUN DELIVERED AS ONE JUMP — the `[ptrinstall]` line measured IDENTITY and Peter's complaint is FLUIDITY.** Flight 11 (2026-09-22, Peter: "mouse not fluid, jumping around, sticky") ends `installs=4873 reports=4873 lag_max_ms=744 coalesced=2 drains=1859 folds=2950` — the B117 identity holds on all 166 samples, which is exactly why the line could not explain the complaint. TWO MECHANISMS, NAMED FROM THE CODE. (1) THE DRAIN AND THE PRESENT ARE ONE TASK ON ONE CORE: `x86_render_service` blocks on `recv`, drains a burst, breaks on empty, and only THEN runs `pal.render()` — so nothing is dispatched while a present runs and the drain cadence IS the present cadence. Differenced across the capture, the storm window dispatches relative reports at **0.4-2.7/s while reports arrive at 10-50/s** (`d_installs=255 d_drains=29 d_folds=257` over 5.1 s; one sample `d_installs=15 d_drains=0`), i.e. the focused app is told where the pointer is one to three times a second, each time by one dispatch carrying the folded sum. `presents=4727` over ~998 s is the same number from the other side: a ~211 ms mean loop period. (2) **B117'S OWN REGRESSION:** `x86_ptr_install`'s first statement was `let fb = *video::WRITER.lock()` — a BLOCKING acquire of a raw `spin::Mutex` **on the preemptible input band**, the exact boot-8 shape LOCKFIX removed from `click_pointer_pos` one function over (rmbp-ledger B1) and which `video/mod.rs`'s door comment already forbade the input path. B117 moved the install onto the input core and carried the acquire with it, and the input service is also the SOLE drain of `pal::EVENT_QUEUE` — so a blocked install stops the ring, the ring backs up, the channel fills and the consumer folds the backlog: **the fold storm and the install stall share one cause.** FIX (this arc, `main.rs` only): the geometry read goes through `video::panel_info_nonblocking` — the counted non-blocking door `video/mod.rs` documents as "the ONE panel acquisition the input path makes" — with the last good geometry cached in `PTRI_PANEL_WH`, so a refusal degrades to the same number taken earlier rather than to a lost install (panel geometry changes only on a mode set). | B168 | **THE X86 KERNEL NUMBERED ITS INTERRUPT VECTORS BY HAND, AND TWO DRIVERS THAT PICKED THE SAME NUMBER WOULD HAVE COLLIDED IN SILENCE — `idt[v].set_handler_fn` IS A PLAIN OVERWRITE AND THE WIRE CANNOT TELL A STOLEN VECTOR FROM A DEVICE THAT NEVER INTERRUPTED.** Five `pub const`s at the top of `arch/x86_64/interrupts.rs` WERE the allocation policy (`XHCI_MSI_VECTOR 0x40`, `NIC_MSI_VECTOR 0x41`, `IPI_VECTOR 0x42`, `EHCI_MSI_VECTOR 0x43`, and their own comments say how they were chosen — *"0x41 is reserved for the NIC, so IPIs use 0x42"*), each registered by name in the IDT and named AGAIN by the driver that programmed its MSI (`pci.rs:779`/`:940`, `drivers/ehci/mod.rs:15172`) or, since IOAPIC (B147), its redirection entry. The defect was already written down from the other side: rmbp-queue's KVBLANK row reads *"`arch/x86_64/interrupts.rs` has three hard-coded IDT vectors and **no allocator a PCI function can join**"*. The next asker — the HDA completion (B152's 1210 ms tone test is entirely polled), an AHCI port (B89), a second EHCI/xHCI function, the UVC isochronous pipe under CAMERA2 — would have copied the pattern and picked by eye. **BUILT: `interrupts::vectors`, one table, one mutex, no heap** (it runs at `init_idt`, long before `memory::init`). `reserve(vector, name)` records the three numbers this kernel cannot move (`timer` 0x20, `ipi` 0x42, `spurious` 0xFF — `apic.rs` arms the timer from the first, `smp.rs`/`sched.rs` build the ICR word from the second, and the third IS the SVR low byte); `alloc(name, handler)` takes the lowest free vector at or above `FLOOR` and **registers the IDT entry BEFORE returning the number**, so a caller can never program a device with a vector whose entry is not yet live; `of(name)` is how a driver asks — there is no const left to name. The IDT is now mutable after `lidt` (an `UnsafeCell`, pointer published by `init_idt`) and THAT is what makes the allocator joinable by a driver that probes late instead of only by `interrupts.rs`; writing a descriptor of a loaded IDT is defined because the CPU reads the entry at DELIVERY, and the entry `alloc` writes is not deliverable until its caller programs the device with the number it just returned. **THE WIRE DOES NOT MOVE, AND THAT IS THE ARC'S CENTRAL CLAIM: the three existing vectors are the allocator's FIRST THREE ANSWERS, seeded IN THE IDT INITIALIZER — `xhci` 0x40, `nic` 0x41, `ehci` 0x43** (0x42 is `ipi`, reserved before the first `alloc` runs, so the third answer skips it). **The seeding site is the only place that order can be pinned, and that is a MEASUREMENT not a preference**: the drivers probe EHCI -> xHCI -> NIC (`pci::init` calls `ehci::init` above the xHCI scan and `init_network()` last), so an allocator asked at each driver's own MSI site would have answered `ehci` 0x40 and renumbered three vectors for nothing. `FLOOR` is 0x40 rather than `RANGE_LO` 0x30 for that reason and one more: a vector's priority class on x86 is its number >> 4 (SDM Vol. 3 §10.8.3), so the low band is where a DELIBERATELY low-priority device belongs, not where the next arrival lands by accident. **CENSUS, one line per boot, printed from the IDT initializer**: `[vectors] allocated=3 free=172 table=timer:0x20,xhci:0x40,nic:0x41,ipi:0x42,ehci:0x43,spurious:0xff == witness ::`. It is there rather than after the last driver arms BECAUSE THERE IT IS UNCONDITIONAL — every vector this kernel hands out is allocated while the IDT is CONSTRUCTED, so the table is complete at `init_idt` and the line reaches the wire of the default image that boots the metal whether or not a NIC, an xHCI or an EHCI was found. A census at a driver's arm site could not promise that: this laptop's NIC is a Broadcom part that takes `init_network`'s non-Intel early exit on EVERY boot, upstream of the MSI-enable site. A runtime `alloc` re-prints the census, so the LAST `[vectors]` line of any capture is always the final table. `free=172` is what `alloc` could still hand out (176 slots in 0x40..=0xEF less the four owned), not a restatement of the range. **NO `knoboff` VERDICT IS QUOTED, deliberately**: the allocator replaces unconditional code with unconditional code and LAWS §5 (2026-09-22) says knob-off identity cannot certify such a change. The proof is the REPLAY. **DEFAULT LANE `./arroyo test 240`, base at the parent `2495f3a2` vs after, both rc=0, spec 6/6 -> 7/7:** `[e1000] RX interrupt (MSI vector 0x41): enabled` on both — SAME VECTOR; `xHCI: [IRQ] xHCI interrupts taken so far:` 35 -> 30 and `[e1000] RX #18 … irqs=18` -> `#36 … irqs=30`. **THOSE TWO COUNTERS ARE NOT BYTE-COMPARABLE AND THIS ROW DOES NOT PRETEND THEY ARE**: they count packets and completions over a boot whose length host load sets, and the base reached completion at +24.8 s against the after run's +103.5 s on a bench at load 20+, which is the whole of 18 -> 36. What is comparable is that both ISRs are armed at the SAME vector, both counters move OFF ZERO, and `irqs=` still tracks `RX #` with the polled drain's small lag — a stolen vector reads `irqs=0` with `RX #` climbing and neither capture does. The sharper row is the EHCI's: `:: EHCI-HID: [0] ISRARM REFUSED — this function offers no usable MSI capability …` is present CHARACTER FOR CHARACTER on both, which is the new `None` arm being UNREACHABLE measured rather than asserted (the allocated vector existed; QEMU's `hcd-ehci` capability list did not). **IOAPIC REPLAY (B147's own lane, where the EHCI vector is actually used), rc=0**, B147's invocation on a port of its own (`UNAOS_IOAPIC=1 UNAOS_QEMU_EXTRA="-qmp tcp:127.0.0.1:4493,server,nowait" ./arroyo test 150` + `scripts/qmp_type.py --port 4493 --marker ':: EHCI-HID: [0] M2 armed keyboard' --bursts 6 --burst 9`): `[ioapic] armed bdf=0:3.0 gsi=11 vector=0x43 dest_apic=0 entry=0x0000000000018043 unmasked_lo=0x00008043 intx_disable=0 routed=1` — **byte-identical to the line B147 recorded**, `entry=` and `unmasked_lo=` and all, except that `vector=0x43` is now an ALLOCATED number and `route_pci_function` takes it from `vectors::of("ehci")` instead of a const. Then `:: EHCI-HID: [0] ISRARM armed — MSI vector 0x43 -> apic 0xfee00000 …` and `:: EHCI-HID: ISRARM armed=1 refused=0 irq=72 isr_rearm=64 poll_rearm=8 depth_max=8 ringfull=8 …` — `irq=` OFF ZERO with 64 of 72 re-arms from the ISR, which is B147's own pass criterion. One `ISRARM IRQ DEAD … in 6033 ms (irq=0 …)` precedes them and must: the self-check fires while the controller is armed and the typist has not started. B147's GO-RED was that line TWICE with ZERO rollups; here it is once, followed by three. **GO-RED, SCRATCH PROBE, RUN AND REVERTED BEFORE THE COMMIT** — a `vectors::scratch_probe()` at the end of `init_idt` doing the collision and then the same ask through the allocator, rc=0: `[vectors] SCRATCH before-allocator: idt[0x40] handler 0x3c53c5f0 -> 0x3c53c3e0 — TWO NAMES ON ONE VECTOR … The overwrite SUCCEEDED, xhci's ISR will never run again, and nothing on the wire says so ==` / `[vectors] SCRATCH restored: idt[0x40] handler 0x3c53c5f0 (== 0x3c53c5f0)` / `[vectors] alloc name=xhci -> REFUSED reason=duplicate-name held=0x40 kind=allocated — that name already owns a vector, and a second registration would OVERWRITE its IDT entry …` / `[vectors] SCRATCH after-allocator: alloc("xhci") -> None`. **The two handler addresses are the whole argument**: `set_handler_fn` SUCCEEDED and moved the entry from `xhci_msi_handler` to `nic_msi_handler`, and the pre-allocator kernel would have printed nothing at all. `kind=` distinguishes the two mistakes (`allocated` vs `reserved`). **SPEC GO-RED, no QEMU run needed**: the new `x86-default.spec` rule replayed against the base capture — the run that has no allocator in it — `rc=1`, `6/7`, naming itself `FIRST-SHORTFALL x86-default.spec:139 REQUIRE \[vectors\] allocated=…`. No FORBID partner, on B160's measurement rather than taste: a FORBID that can no longer match reads ✅ with 0 hits and is indistinguishable from one that passed, while the failure here is a vector silently changing, which a REQUIRE on the exact table convicts. **LINE-NEUTRAL WHERE IT HAD TO BE**: `drivers/ehci/mod.rs` is **18921 lines before and after** (B94 same-line folds; that file is 18k lines of `panic::Location` and B147's byte-identity claim rides on them). `pci.rs` and `interrupts.rs` are not line-constrained and were not folded. ⚠ **FOUND, NOT FIXED, AND NOT MINE:** `drivers/gpu/kepler_vblank.rs:59` still names all three deleted consts in a module comment (`XHCI_MSI_VECTOR` 0x40, `NIC_MSI_VECTOR` 0x41, `EHCI_MSI_VECTOR`). It compiles — they are prose — and the NUMBERS it quotes are still right. It belongs to the KVBLANK arc. ⚠ **WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO:** it renumbers nothing (that is the point); it gives NO device a new interrupt — three drivers stop naming a const and start asking, and HDA/AHCI/UVC are still polled with somewhere to join; it does not free 0x30–0x3F; and it does not stop a future driver from programming a number it invented — nothing in the CPU can. What is gone is the REASON to: there is no const to copy and there is a table to ask. | rmbp | x86 QEMU (`./arroyo test`, and `UNAOS_IOAPIC=1 ./arroyo test` for the EHCI vector) | fixed-unflown — gated on QEMU q35 end to end with three go-reds (the collision probe, the spec pin, and B147's own lane replayed). | B165 | **DOCKID'S TWO DEFECTS WERE A WRITER THAT RANKED AGAINST A MODEL IT HAD ALREADY STOPPED HOLDING, AND A FIXTURE THAT SCORED A REGISTRY NO PASS HAD WRITTEN — AND NEITHER IS THE READER-SIDE SNAPSHOT B150 SPECIFIED.** B159 refused to write that snapshot and said why; this row executes the two fixes it priced instead, and adds a third finding neither brief saw. **(1) THE RANK'S PROVENANCE — FIXED.** `reconcile` was handed `(rows, n)` by `settle`, the model `compose` scanned at the TOP of the pass, so anything allocated after that scan was invisible to the reconcile that followed and was admitted by the NEXT pass beside whatever had arrived since — `gored-b3-serial.log:1219..1238`, `idC` allocated at 1219, not admitted at 1224, `census tiles=4` at 1227 with `idC` LIVE AND TILELESS, then `idD seq=17` and `idC seq=18`, the ELDER window given the LATER rank against a green boot's 17/18 (`g2-test-x86-wc.log:2022/2032`). `reconcile` now takes NO model: it calls `wm::dock_scan` itself immediately before it mutates. | B143 | **THE CAMERA HAS BEEN ON THE BUS OF EVERY BOOT THIS KERNEL HAS EVER TAKEN, AND TWO LINES ARE ITS ENTIRE HISTORY.** Flight 11 (2026-09-22), verbatim: `:: EHCI-HID: [0] M1 hub-downstream device addr=2 05ac:8510 class=0xef speed=HS depth=1 (parent hub 1 port 1) tt=(hub 0 port 0) == witness ::` then `:: EHCI-HID: [0] addr 2 has no HID interrupt-IN endpoint — nothing to arm ::`. The load-bearing field is `class=0xef`, not the vendor id: USB 2.0's IAD ECN uses 0xEF for a device whose interfaces are grouped into FUNCTIONS, and a camera's Interface Association Descriptor carries `bFunctionClass = CC_VIDEO (0x0E)` \[UVC 1.1 §3.5 Table 3-1\]. `configure_hid` matched neither, found no HID interrupt-IN endpoint, and dropped the device — on every boot, for the life of the project. **CAMERA1 BUILDS THE FIRST RUNG: the census and the PROBE negotiation, CONTROL TRANSFERS ONLY** (`drivers/uvc.rs`, new; ONE line folded into `configure_hid`, line-neutral, 18105 lines before and after). It reads the configuration descriptor through the same `control()` helper the HID walk and the bt-l0 census use, walks the VideoControl interface (header, camera input terminal with its controls bitmap, processing unit, output terminal) and every VideoStreaming interface (input header, each format with its frame descriptors' geometry and interval table or range) plus every alternate setting's isochronous IN endpoint, then runs GET_MIN / GET_MAX / GET_DEF / SET_CUR / GET_CUR on `VS_PROBE_CONTROL` \[UVC 1.1 §4.3.1.1 Table 4-47\] and prints the negotiated block field by field with an explicit `agreed=` comparison, because a device is entitled to answer with a format, frame or interval other than the one asked for. **THREE THINGS ARE REFUSED ON PURPOSE AND EACH HAS A LINE:** no isochronous pipe is opened (this driver has no iTD/siTD path and PROBE-14 keeps every transfer on the periodic-QH discipline), `VS_COMMIT_CONTROL` is never sent (`[uvc] commit=withheld reason=no-iso-pipe` — a committed format with nothing draining it leaves the camera armed for the rest of the boot on the controller the internal keyboard is on), and no `SET_CUR` reaches a VideoControl control — brightness, exposure and focus are read as capability BITMAPS \[UVC 1.1 Tables 3-6, 3-8\] and never written. The one state change is the SET_CONFIGURATION that makes an interface-recipient class request legal at all \[USB 2.0 §9.4.3\], and it is reported. Every transfer is issued EXACTLY ONCE; a stall names its stage and its request code and ends the sequence, because the failure this device can inflict is a retry storm on the controller the keyboard enumerates through. **WHAT THE PARSER IS PROVEN BY, since QEMU models no UVC device:** `parse()` is a pure function over a descriptor slice and `selftest()` drives it over a hand-built descriptor set written byte by byte out of the spec's tables — config, video IAD, VC { header bcdUVC 0x0100 clock 6 MHz, camera terminal 0x0201 with a 3-byte bitmap, processing unit with a 2-byte bitmap, output terminal }, VS alt 0 { input header 2 formats ep 0x81, uncompressed YUY2 16 bpp with frame 1 640x480 DISCRETE (2 intervals) and frame 2 1280x720 CONTINUOUS, MJPEG with frame 1 1920x1080 }, VS alt 1 { isochronous IN, two isochronous IN alternates at wMaxPacketSize 0x0C00 and 0x1400 plus an isochronous OUT alternate that must NOT enter the census } — every number distinct from every other so a mis-read offset cannot alias a correct one. ~70 assertions plus a `build_probe`/`parse_probe` round trip, a synthetic device REPLY block with a distinct value in all six fields, and a runt block that must be refused. **GO-RED MEASURED, 26 MUTATIONS AND 26 RED, 0 SURVIVORS**, on a host harness that compiles the parser, fixture and assertions VERBATIM out of this file (only `serial_println!` becomes `println!`; the recipe is three commands in uvc.md §6): unmutated `:: uvc: selftest fixture=289B formats=2 frames=3 alts=2 probe_roundtrip=ok probe_reply=ok -> PASS ::` rc=0, and e.g. `width 5->6` rc=1 `first=fmt0.frame0.width got=57346 want=640`, `payload 22->21` rc=1 `first=probe.reply.max_payload got=786432 want=3072`, `ep dir mask drop` rc=1 `first=alts got=3 want=2`. **THAT SWEEP ALSO CONVICTED THE FIRST DRAFT OF THIS SELF-TEST FOUR TIMES AND EACH FIX IS IN THE FIXTURE WITH ITS REASON:** the probe round trip compared 0 to 0 at both `dwMaxVideoFrameSize` and `dwMaxPayloadTransferSize` because `build_probe` leaves them zero; and with only IN endpoints present, deleting the `d[2] & 0x80` direction test changed nothing — a parser that would have offered the next rung an OUT pipe to read from. It settles NOTHING about the in-kernel path. **WHAT FLIGHT 12 MUST PRINT, and the first number to read is `wTotalLength=` on `[uvc] candidate`:** `control()` reads into `qh::Buf256`, 256 bytes, and USB offers no offset on GET_DESCRIPTOR, so 256 is a hard ceiling on the census window; a camera's configuration descriptor is routinely larger. | B140 | **CMD25 IS IN THE DRIVER AND THE CARD IS STILL `ro`, BECAUSE THE POSTURE HAS ONE DEFINITION AND IT IS NOT IN ANY FILE THIS ARC MAY TOUCH.** SDHCWRITE built milestone 4b's driver half: `sdhc::write_blocks_512`, one polled CMD25 WRITE_MULTIPLE_BLOCK closed by the controller's Auto CMD12 STOP_TRANSMISSION, mirroring the CMD18 read path, plus a four-block fixture that stashes, writes, verifies by CMD18 read-back, restores and verifies the restore. **The CMD25 sequence and its citations** (SD Host Controller Simplified Specification 3.00 for the registers, SD Physical Layer Simplified Specification for the card): CMD25 R1 data-present host->card, Physical Layer §4.3.3 — the card accepts blocks until stopped and signals busy on DAT0 when its write buffer is full; Transfer Mode Multi/Single Block Select = 1 and Block Count Enable = 1 with `TM_DIR_READ` OMITTED, Host Controller §2.2.5 — there is no positive write bit, the ABSENCE of the direction bit is the write; Auto CMD12 (§2.2.5) issues the STOP, so Block Count Enable is not optional and an Auto-CMD12 failure sets error-half bit 8 with its reason in Auto CMD Error Status (§2.2.18), printed raw on every failure line because a failed STOP leaves the CARD streaming; DAT0 programming-busy under Physical Layer §4.6.2.2; CMD13 SEND_STATUS afterwards (§4.10.1) because programming-phase failures raise NO controller interrupt and `prg` carries no error bit. **The timeout correction is the engineering.** §4.6.2.2 states the WRITE timeout as a PER-BLOCK 250 ms. `DATA_TIMEOUT_MS` is 200 ms and is a READ bound (the 100 ms read-access ceiling doubled) — BELOW the spec's own write figure. A CMD25 path copying CMD18's shape would convict a legal card of a timeout the first time it went busy on a full write buffer, i.e. a first CMD25 failing for a reason that is not CMD25. Every wait card programming can hold off now uses `mb_write_budget_ms(count) = PROG_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS * count`, saturating. **Gates kept.** 1 build (`#[cfg(feature = "sdw")]` — no CMD25 and no CMD12 word in a default image, 4a's property extended to two more commands), 2 the write-protect PIN re-read from Present State bit 19 at the moment of THIS write, 3 the card's own CSD PERM/TMP_WRITE_PROTECT, 4 the blank proof — re-made PER BLOCK, as is the partition-extent test, because a window is only as safe as its least safe sector. | B154 | **THE SERIAL CONSOLE NO LONGER MASKS INTERRUPTS TO WRITE ITS OWN LINE ON x86 — AND THE FIRST MEASUREMENT REFUTES B146's MECHANISM SENTENCE ON THE ONE BOARD IT WAS WRITTEN FOR: THE rMBP HAS NO 16550.** (1) **MEASURED FIRST, AND THE MEASUREMENT RE-SCOPED THE BRIEF.** B146 named `serial::_print` masking interrupts and draining the ring "through a 16550 a byte at a time" as the owner of `max=108ms`. That cannot be the site on this laptop, and flight 11's own wire says so three independent ways: `[244ms] :: SERWIT-1: contended serial [uart16550=absent carrier=ftdi-mirror law=emitted==0] … (submitted=151 emitted=0 declined=151 inflight=0) -> PASS ::`; `[28280ms] :: DRAINCAP: SKIP — no 16550 on this machine, nothing is ever staged (SERWIT-1D) ::`; and `wcd_us=0 wcd_skips=0` on every `[comp2]` rollup of the flight. With no 16550 every masked branch of `_print` on that board is the O(1) `DECLINED` one: nothing staged, nothing drained, not one byte written behind the mask. The CORRELATION B146 measured is untouched and is re-derived here independently, forward from the capture's timestamps rather than from `[deadman] pmp=`: bucketing all 18 290 lines into whole seconds gives **24 seconds at >=150 lines/s against 957 below 50, over 999 s** — the same burst structure §33h partitioned 928 s into. So the console is still the suspect; what is refuted is the SITE, and the census is built to name it. (2) **THE FOUR TERMS, AND ONLY ONE HAD EVER HAD AN INSTRUMENT.** A `_print` pays the ring drain (SO29 capped it, SO45 measures it), the OWN-LINE synchronous emission, the contended-lock spin, and the four POST-MASK taps. Terms 2-4 had no counter anywhere. Term 2 is the big one on a machine that has a UART: 115200 8N1 is 86.8 us/byte, so a 100-byte line is **~8.7 ms with interrupts masked**, on top of the <=22.6 ms SO31's cap allows — `DRAIN_BYTE_BUDGET` bounded the SMALLER of the two masked costs. (3) **THE FIX (x86_64 only).** `_print` ENQUEUES its line: the masked region is a compare-exchange and a memcpy and emits ZERO UART bytes; `SERIAL1` is taken there only to ask once per boot whether a 16550 exists and, where it does not, to hold the drainer's uniqueness across `discard_staged` (SERWIT-1D accounting unchanged). A DRAIN OWNER with interrupts ENABLED (`drain_owner()`) then emits up to `DRAIN_BYTE_BUDGET`. **The owner is WHICHEVER CORE PRINTS NEXT**, with `serial_ring::mirror_service` (main-loop polled, IF=1, lock-free) as the residual flush when printing stops. Chosen over the two alternatives ON THE MERITS and not only because they need foreign files: the 1 kHz tick is `arch/x86_64/interrupts.rs` (IOAPIC's) and the 1 ms `x86_usb_pump` is `main.rs` (NEUTRAL's) — **STOP-REPORTED, one call each, not written** — and both would move the console's cost ONTO service core c7, which is precisely the core EHCIDARK is trying to protect, while the next-printer owner is self-clocking (a console under load has a next print by definition) and reserves nothing. A print that ARRIVED masked (ISR, exception, another subsystem's `without_interrupts`) cannot unmask, so it takes exactly one 16550 transmit FIFO — `MASKED_BYTE_BUDGET` = 16 B = 1.39 ms worst case — and leaves the rest. ORDERING is unchanged and now structural (every line goes through the ring, so wire order IS submission order and there is no direct line left to reorder against); LOSS is unchanged branch for branch (`defer_contended`, `BACKPRESSURE_SPINS`, counted `DROPPED`, announced marker) — what moved is WHERE a retry turn makes progress: out of the mask. Panic and power keep their UNCAPPED synchronous drains. (4) **THE CENSUS, UNCONDITIONAL ON PURPOSE.** `[sertx] prints= masked_us_max= masked_us_mean= drain_us= emit_us= spin_us= bytes= masked_b= fifo_b= taps_us= taps_us_max= sink= hz= masked_cy_max= masked_cy_sum=`, rolled up every 10 s out of `mirror_service`. NOT `witness`-gated, because the images that produce dark windows are the ones built witness-FREE (`esp-x86` media, LAWS §5's default-quiet polarity rule) — a gated `[sertx]` would be absent from every image that has ever produced one. It reports the POST-MASK taps BESIDE the masked terms rather than folding them in, which is the whole reason it can say anything on the rMBP at all. Cost: two `now_cycles()` reads and a handful of relaxed atomics per print. ⚠ **IT MOVES THE DEFAULT IMAGE AND `knoboff` SAYS SO**: `./arroyo knoboff wc cb3f3ba0` and `knoboff logts cb3f3ba0` both exit **1**, `warm=yes`, control fired on BOTH arches, x86 1 606 680 -> 1 609 920 B and arm 1 601 385 -> 1 601 977 B with the tool's own reading `the SIZE changed, so this is code, not a line shift`. That is the correct verdict for a behaviour change in unconditional console code, and it is why the proof is the QEMU run and not the byte compare. (5) **aarch64 IS MEASURED, NOT CHANGED.** That arch still drains and then writes its own line inside the mask; every statement this arc adds there is a counter read. `[sertx] emit_us` non-zero and `masked_b` tracking the line width IS the second milestone's evidence, and the port is decided by those numbers rather than by symmetry. | B163 | **EVERY CHORD THE DESKTOP UNDERSTANDS IS A ROW IN A TABLE THE THEME OWNS, AND ONE RESOLVER READS IT — R60 AND R61, DELIVERED AS FAR AS THE RESOLVER AND NOT ONE STEP FURTHER.** **(1) WHAT WAS A LITERAL.** `drivers/xhci/mod.rs`'s `hid_screenshot_chord_edge` tested `HID_MOD_GUI` and `HID_MOD_SHIFT` and usages `0x20`/`0x21` INLINE, the EHCI decoder called that same function, and Print Screen was a second literal (`0x46`) beside it; the `HID_USAGE_DIGIT_3`/`_4` consts lived in the USB driver. A Windows-shaped theme could not be added without editing two USB drivers, which is what R60 forbids. **(2) WHAT IS A TABLE NOW.** `video/keymap.rs` (NEW): `Action` (`Screenshot`, `ScreenshotRegion`, `Copy`, `Cut`, `Paste`, `SelectAll`, `LogOut`), `Binding { roles, usage, action, token }`, `Table { name, cmd_role, rows }`, and ONE resolver — `resolve(table, modifiers, usage_edge)`, with `resolve_chord` as its witness face (the same single walk) and `resolve_edge` as its report-pair face. **THE SEAM IS ONE FIELD WIDE: `cmd_role`**, the PHYSICAL HID mask that plays the abstract `CMD` role. `⌘C` is written once, as `CMD` ORed with usage `0x06`; `theme::CRISPY_BINDINGS` says `CMD` is `HID_MOD_GUI` and `theme::PC_BINDINGS` says it is `HID_MOD_ALT`, and no row anywhere names a physical modifier. The rows live at the TAIL of `video/theme.rs` because a chord is a property of the theme exactly as a colour is (R60's own words). Both decoders now ask and never test: `hid_screenshot_chord_edge` is a hand-off to `keymap::resolve_edge`, `hid_print_screen_action_edge` resolves the 0x46 edge's MEANING through the same table (so a theme with no Print Screen row disarms the key), and the two `HID_USAGE_DIGIT_*` consts are deleted. **(3) R61 NEEDS NO GUARD, AND THAT IS THE POINT.** `Ctrl-C` keeps its byte-0x03 meaning in the shell because THE TABLE NEVER CLAIMS IT — `CTRL` is a role the resolver understands and no shipped row uses it. | B147 | **THIS KERNEL HAD NO I/O APIC AT ALL, SO EVERY PCI FUNCTION WITHOUT AN MSI CAPABILITY COULD ONLY BE POLLED — AND THE EHCI CONTROLLERS ARE THE MEASURED CASE.** THE WIRE FIRST: flight 11, `f11.log` 25626 ms, `:: EHCI-HID: [1] ISRARM REFUSED — this function offers no usable MSI capability, and there is no IOAPIC in this kernel to route INTx to. The endpoint stays on the POLLED re-arm path … ::`. That refusal was ACCURATE IN EVERY WORD, and this row is its repeal. `arch/x86_64/apic.rs` is 498 lines of LOCAL APIC (xAPIC MMIO + the x2APIC MSR bank) with no redirection-entry writer anywhere in the tree; `drivers/pci.rs` can enable MSI and MSI-X and nothing else; `interrupts::disable_legacy_pic` masks every 8259 line and `apic::init` leaves LINT0 masked, so there was no virtual-wire path either. A function could assert INTA# and the assertion went NOWHERE. The cost is B139's: `EHCIDARK … kind=vendor-mt reports=5706 … dark=13646ms max=108ms missed<=11384`. **BUILT — three rungs behind ONE knob `UNAOS_IOAPIC=1` / feature `ioapic`, each committed green before the next, in a NEW file `arch/x86_64/ioapic.rs` plus two LINE-NEUTRAL sites in `arch/x86_64/acpi.rs` and ONE in `drivers/ehci/mod.rs`.** **(1) CENSUS.** `acpi::parse_madt` matches exactly two entry types (Local APIC 0, Local x2APIC 9) and drops the rest into `_ => {}` — which is where the I/O APIC (ACPI §5.2.12.3), Interrupt Source Override (§5.2.12.5) and Local APIC NMI (§5.2.12.7) entries have been going SINCE THE FILE WAS WRITTEN. That arm now feeds a collector; the topology walk above it is untouched. Each controller's IOREGSEL/IOWIN window is mapped (`map_mmio_window`, called rather than assumed) and IOAPICVER read. Nothing is written. Three things it gets right on purpose: IOAPICVER bits 23:16 are the MAXIMUM REDIRECTION ENTRY — the LAST VALID INDEX — so the COUNT is that PLUS ONE (off by one silently refuses the highest GSI on the machine); `0xFFFFFFFF` is an unclaimed MMIO read, so such a controller is `REFUSED reason=ioapicver-unreadable` and left at `entries = 0`, which `locate` then makes structurally UNROUTABLE rather than routable-and-unprovable; and `dropped=` counts entries the fixed tables could not hold, so a machine bigger than this module SAYS so. **(2) ROUTE.** `route_gsi` programs one 64-bit entry per 82093AA §3.2.4 — vector, delivery Fixed, destination physical, polarity, trigger, **MASK SET** — high dword first so the dword carrying the vector and the mask latches last, then READS IT BACK and compares (bits 12/14 are the controller's read-only status and are excluded). Masked-then-`set_mask` is not a detail: an entry live the instant it is written can deliver to a vector whose handler the caller has not finished preparing. `route_pci_intx` derives the GSI from the function's OWN Interrupt Pin/Line registers (PCI 3.0 §6.2.4) through the override table, defaulting to PCI's polarity and trigger — LEVEL, ACTIVE LOW (§2.2.6) — not ISA's. **(3) PCI ARM.** `route_pci_function` is the `&& !…` term added to `isr_arm_controller`'s MSI condition: route MASKED, clear PCI COMMAND bit 10 (Interrupt Disable, §6.2.2) and read it back, THEN unmask — in that order, because an entry routed correctly to a function that cannot assert is a perfect route and a dead interrupt, the quietest way this fails. NO HANDLER, NO VECTOR AND NO IDT ENTRY WERE ADDED and `interrupts.rs` is untouched: the completion vector (0x43), its IDT entry and `ehci_msi_handler` are the ones ISRARM already had, and only the DELIVERY PATH is new. No EOI special case either — a level entry's Remote IRR is cleared by the LOCAL APIC's EOI broadcast (SDM Vol. 3 §10.8.5; 82093AA §3.2.4) and every handler already writes EOI last. **MEASURED ON QEMU q35**, whose `hcd-ehci` advertises no PCI capability list, so `enable_msi` refuses and this is the INTx path end to end: `[ioapic] census ioapics=1 isos=5 gsis=24 nmis=1 dropped=0 madt_entries=7`, `[ioapic] id=0 addr=0xfec00000 gsi_base=0 entries=24 version=0x20`, `[ioapic] route bdf=0:3.0 pin=INTD line=11 -> gsi=11 via=iso polarity=active-high trigger=level`, `[ioapic] armed bdf=0:3.0 gsi=11 vector=0x43 dest_apic=0 entry=0x0000000000018043 unmasked_lo=0x00008043 intx_disable=0 routed=1`. **SCORED ON INSTRUMENTS THAT ALREADY EXISTED** so a new counter cannot let the old one rot — the ISRARM rollup's `irq=` and the existing `ISRARM IRQ DEAD` self-check: `:: EHCI-HID: ISRARM armed=1 refused=0 irq=122 isr_rearm=109 poll_rearm=13 depth_max=8 ringfull=10 cont_isr=3 cont_poll=1 oversize=0 ::` — **109 of 122 endpoint re-arms came from the ISR instead of the polled pass**, which is the arc's whole product. **GO-RED, RUN AND REVERTED** (`set_mask(gsi, true)` — leave the entry masked; same lane, same 120 typed events): `unmasked_lo=0x00018043` with bit 16 still set, **ZERO** `ISRARM armed=` rollups and TWO `ISRARM IRQ DEAD … irq=0 isr_rearm=0` lines — THE ROUTE CORRECT AND THE INTERRUPT DEAD, exactly the pair a gate scoring the route alone would have passed. **THE LANE, because a bare run measures `irq=0` HONESTLY:** the one QEMU usb-kbd rides the usb-ehci harness controller by default (`UNAOS_XHCIKBD` is what moves it to xHCI), but nothing types at it and an interrupt-IN endpoint that NACKs completes no qTD. The run pairs the default lane with a QMP typist ON A PORT OF ITS OWN — `UNAOS_IOAPIC=1 UNAOS_QEMU_EXTRA="-qmp tcp:127.0.0.1:4489,server,nowait" ./arroyo test 150` + `scripts/qmp_type.py --port 4489 --marker ':: EHCI-HID: [0] M2 armed keyboard' --bursts 6 --burst 9` — because QEMU's `-qmp …,server,nowait` accepts ONE client and riding `UNAOS_QMP_SHOT`'s socket gets a TCP accept and no greeting (one run lost to exactly that). ⚠ **WHAT THIS RUNG CANNOT ANSWER, stated on the wire and not buried:** the DSDT `_PRT` is the authoritative PCI routing table and it is AML; this kernel has no interpreter. So the GSI comes from firmware's own Interrupt Line, and an unprogrammed line (0x00/0xFF) is `REFUSED reason=no-firmware-line` — nothing written, the driver keeps polling, and the flight-11 refusal STAYS on the wire for that case. Closing it needs an AML interpreter or an ICH9 / 7-series `PIRQ[A-H]_ROUT` decode; both are their own arcs | rmbp | rmbp | fixed-unflown — gated on QEMU q35 end to end with its go-red; the METAL half is flight 12 and is the row's open half. **FLIGHT 12 MUST PRINT:** `[ioapic] census ioapics=1 … gsis=24` with `[ioapic] id=… addr=0xfec00000 … entries=24` — the 7-series PCH is EXPECTED to carry one I/O APIC at that address with 24 entries, stated here so the flight can CONTRADICT it; the EHCI functions' `[ioapic] route bdf=… line=<n>` values AS THE WIRE REPORTS THEM (a `line=255` is itself the finding — firmware routed the function nowhere — and sends the question to the `_PRT` paragraph above); and what happens to `EHCIDARK … kind=vendor-mt … dark= max= missed<=` against B139's `dark=13646ms max=108ms missed<=11384` once a completion interrupt can arm. | B153 | **x86 HAD NO BUS AT ALL, AND WHAT MADE THAT HARD TO SEE IS THAT IT WAS NOT A MISSING DRIVER BUT A MISSING HALF OF A SYSCALL TABLE.** BANDY-1/BANDY-2 shipped `SYS_MSEND`/`SYS_MRECV`, bounded mailboxes, kernel-stamped principals and in-kernel `ls`/`cat`/`cp` fulfilment — all of it inside `arch/aarch64/`. On this board `grep` found neither verb number in `arch/x86_64/syscall.rs`, so STAT, VUG and PULSE, the three EL0 programs this track actually ships, had nothing to speak on. M2 lands the x86 half against the codec SR20 made shared. **THE TRANSPORT IS A PORT AND SAYS WHERE IT IS NOT.** Identical to the Pi's: capacity checked BEFORE fulfillment (`-EAGAIN`, so a side-effectful verb can never run and lose its reply), depth 16 per row, synchronous fulfilment in the caller's own syscall context under the invoker's grants, `-EMSGSIZE` on a sub-frame `SYS_MRECV` buffer, teardown drain after the generation bump, and a reply stamped with the RESERVED KERNEL record. **THE THREE PLACES aarch64's IMPLEMENTATION LEANS ON SOMETHING x86 DOES NOT HAVE**, each a contract claim rather than a coding detail. (1) THE PRINCIPAL: aarch64 stamps a `PrincipalRecord` from the K-line IMAGE_SHA256 mint; **x86 has no such type and needs none.** Its U6 identity — the one its OWN `SYS_OPEN` owner ACL is keyed on, hence the only identity an equivalence witness could compare against — is `(row, SLOT_GEN[row])`, and that pair is what every fulfiller receives, exactly as aarch64 passes `(asid, agen, ppid)`. This costs the WIRE nothing, and the reason is structural rather than lucky: on aarch64 the stamped SENDER principal is never read off a frame either — `sys_msend_for` requires the field zero, hands `ppid` to the fulfiller directly, and never looks at `hdr.principal` again — so the ONLY principal that reaches the wire in either direction is the reply's reserved KERNEL record, kind 4 / len 0 / value zero, which is a CONSTANT. x86 writes that constant as its 32 wire bytes. The KATs pin those bytes and pass here unmodified. (2) THE MAILBOX ROW: ASID -> the HANDLES row (`caller_row()`), `SHARED_ROW` included, `USER_SLOTS + 1` wide, fenced by `SLOT_GEN` (bumped at the top of `clear_handle_row`, which is why the drain folded in beside `owned_clear_owner_slot` is sufficient and not merely tidy). (3) THE NAMESPACE, and this one is not cosmetic: aarch64 fulfils through `fs::fat` against a real on-disk root keyed `(dir_lba, dir_off)`; x86's EL0 namespace is the STAGED set plus the STATIC `U10_NAMES` table, keyed by NAME-ID, whose "this file exists" test is `created_desc_any_row` — **a live descriptor, not a directory entry.** So the fulfiller re-enters `sys_open`'s own sequence in `sys_open`'s order (root-leaf collapse -> staged -> `SHARED_ROW` -> `DYN_DELETED_G` -> `created_desc_any_row` -> `owned_access_ok`), which is what makes the errnos byte-same BY CONSTRUCTION instead of by a table of hand-copied numbers. **THE ONE HONEST-SCOPE NOTE, STATED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED:** because a created file's identity on x86 IS a live descriptor, a fulfiller that created a copy and closed its own handle would destroy what it had just acknowledged — so bus `cp` does what the DIRECT path does and KEEPS the descriptor (`open_create_new`, private to the invoker, one of its eight handle slots), which is the only shape on this arch that leaves the copy visible to a following `ls`. The BANDY-2 write side (`write`/`rm`/`mv`) DECODES here — the codec is shared, the goldens run — but is not fulfilled: it answers `-ENOSYS` in a well-formed reply rather than `-EINVAL`, so a client can tell "this board cannot do that yet" from "I spoke wrongly". Both want a descriptor-free create/unlink/rename in the x86 created-name namespace, which is the STOR-1 line's work. **WITNESS AND ITS GO-RED, BEHAVIOURAL.** `:: BUSX86-STAMP: SYS_MSEND/SYS_MRECV on x86 — kernel-written principal (caller-supplied REJECTED -EINVAL), replies stamped RESERVED-KERNEL kind=4, errno-in-status-no-body, mailbox bounded per-row depth=16 fail-closed, gen-fenced, identity=(row,SLOT_GEN) :: PASS [w=0x3f/0x3f] ::` — six bits: the caller-supplied principal refused with nothing queued, the reply's echoed verb/corr and the kernel stamp, the staged (public) `cat`, errno-in-status-with-empty-body on `-ENOENT`, a full mailbox refusing the 17th send while a second row is unaffected, and the generation fence discarding a stale reply. GO-RED: delete the `request_validate` clause in `busx_msend_for`, rebuild, boot — `:: BUSX86-STAMP: … :: FAIL [w=0x20/0x3f] ::` (five of six bits lost; the unrefused frame also pollutes the mailbox the later bits pop from). Reverted. **GATES**, all quoted: `cd unaos && ./arroyo check` rc=0 — `✅ kernel cfg coverage OK (80 legs)`, `✅ knob-parity OK`, 161 green markers, 0 red, both arches. `UNAOS_WC=1 UNAOS_QUARRY=1 UNAOS_FTDIRX=1 UNAOS_QEMU_FULL=1 ./arroyo test 240` rc=0, `✅ MBENCH PASS — 6/6 required witnesses, 0 forbidden hit(s), 2838 lines scanned`, boot reached its last fixture at serial.log line 2442, and the three bus lines above. `./arroyo kernel8-test 300` rc=0 `✅ MBENCH PASS — 126/126 required witnesses, 0 forbidden hit(s)` (a FIRST run on a loaded box read 124/126 with `EXEC-UVUG … did not exit in time` and `[wc-k] … torn=2 -> AT-RISK`, both load-sensitive and both green on the re-run — recorded because a flake that is not written down gets re-diagnosed). `./arroyo test-arm` rc=0. ARTIFACT GREPS, `LC_ALL=C grep -a -o -F`: on the x86 kernel `BUSX86-STAMP` 1, `BANDY-CODEC` 4, `BANDY-CODEC2` 2, `UBS1` 19; on the Pi `kernel8.img`, `BUSX86-STAMP` 0, `busx_` 0, `identity=(row,SLOT_GEN)` 0 — the x86 half reaches no aarch64 byte. SIZES: x86 knob-off 1,605,400 -> 1,619,696 B (+14,296); arm knob-off BYTE-IDENTICAL at 1,601,385 B. | rmbp | rmbp | fixed-unflown — QEMU-green on this bench, the rMBP metal leg rides the next attended sitting; branch `exec-rmbp-busx86` off `878e1818` (two commits, M1 then M2 — the seat re-derives the tip at the fold); gates in the commit bodies | this arc's `target/serial.log` (the three bus witnesses and the go-red capture in `busx86-logs/`); `docs/dev/OS/02_KERNEL_CORE/userspace.md` §BUSX86 | -> SR20 |
| B158 | **THE WORST FLAKE ON THE BENCH WAS THE FIXTURE SCORING COMPOSITE PASSES THAT `COMP_GATE` HAD DECLINED — `[dmgovlp] adopt_stretch=0/4 -> FAIL` WITH EVERY OTHER COUNTER ZERO, AND `drained=12/12` SCORED BY THE COMPOSITOR DOING NOTHING.** Rate BEFORE: **6 of 47 boots on 2026-09-22 (~13%)**, FIXTURE_FLAKES §1c's own measurement, the worst of the three flakes measured that day; cost to the fleet: **one lost 25-minute gate run per executor per day**, and §1c could not be touched because `wm.rs` was PTRPAINT's. Rate AFTER: the mechanism is removed rather than made less likely — see the forced-fold row below, which is the only honest way to rate a ~13% event without 47 boots. **MECHANISM (measured, not inferred).** `wm::composite`'s x86 arm compare-exchanges `COMP_GATE`; a second entrant takes the DECLINE arm, whose own comment states it exactly — *“This pass composites nothing and — crucially — CLEARS NOTHING”* — storing `COMP_PENDING`, ticking `WCSER_DECLINED`, calling `owe_repaint()` and returning in microseconds. `dmgovlp_selftest` read that as success twice: every counter it reports is a delta over work that never happened (so `drag_evt`/`drag_px`/`relay`/`narrow`/`adopt`/`adopt_stretch` all read 0), and its drain check — “one extra composite must add NOTHING” — is SATISFIED BY THE DECLINE, so `drained=12/12` was scored by twelve passes that never ran. **THE READING THAT WAS WRONG FOR A MONTH WAS `max_ms`.** §1c predicted starvation and asked for `max_ms` as an outlier; every failing capture reads `max_ms=0..3` against greens at `max_ms=2..25` — the flakes are the FAST runs, because nothing happened in them. Starvation makes a pass slower; this made it instant. **THE PROOF IT IS NOT A CLOCK IS THE BIMODALITY.** A declined battery completes in microseconds, so it fits inside ONE sibling composite pass (`[comp2] pass_us=4265` mean under TCG, 170 ms tail): either the gate is free at entry and all twelve passes run, or it is held and ALL twelve fold. On the bench every green reads `drag_evt=5 drag_px=38590 … adopt_stretch=4/4` and every flake reads `drag_evt=0 drag_px=0 relay=0 narrow=0/12 … adopt_stretch=0/4`; a per-pass wall-clock lottery would have produced 1/4, 2/4 and 3/4 and NONE EXISTS. **THE DISCRIMINATOR WAS FREE ON EVERY CAPTURE ALL ALONG:** the `[wcser]` rollup. Every flake carries `scope=fixture declined_pct=23..31` (`gmux8-logs/test240.log` `entered=107 declined=48 declined_pct=30`; `flakefix-logs/repro1.log` `entered=202 declined=61 declined_pct=23`; `ptrinstall3-logs/serial-smp2-wc.log` `entered=165 declined=75 declined_pct=31`); greens carry `declined_pct=0` or no fixture-scope declines at all. | B155 | **THE INTERNAL SD CARD CAN NOW BE MOUNTED READ-WRITE, THE ANSWER HAS ONE DEFINITION AT LAST, AND WHETHER THE BOOT VOLUME SHOULD BE `rw` BY DEFAULT IS PETER'S — STATED HERE WITH WHAT EACH ANSWER COSTS.** Flight 11: Peter pressed Print Screen and got `:: PRTSCR: REFUSED READ-ONLY (source=sdhc … SDHC-4c)`. Three milestones of write machinery were in the image (4a's CMD24, 4b's CMD25, 4c's permitted extent) and no path ran from a file verb to any of them, because `fat::BlockSource::write_veto`'s `Sdhc` arm returned `Some(…)` unconditionally and every other reader forwards to it. **THE MECHANISM.** `sdhc=rw` iff ALL THREE hold, and a refusal names WHICH failed, on a truth table printed once at the mount: (1) the `sdw-rw` feature is BUILT (`sdw-off`), (2) the write-protect PIN, read AT MOUNT, says enabled (`wp-protected`), (3) the block layer has a live write path (`no-write-path`). Condition 2 is deliberately NOT 4a/4b's read: those re-read Present State bit 19 at every write and still do; the posture's read answers “may this VOLUME be mounted writable” and is answered ONCE, because `write_veto` exists to say no IN ADVANCE, before a multi-step verb gets part-way — and a latch means a posture cannot change under an open file verb because somebody brushed the slider. **THE FINDING B140 DID NOT HAVE: the posture had TWO readers.** `block::handle_write_veto` stated it a second time and `sdwrite_posture_selftest` leg 8 compares the two for every source in `fat::ALL_SOURCES`; lifting the FAT arm alone, as B140 prescribed, prints `sdhc=rw!DISAGREES` + `FAIL ::` and reddens every QEMU run. Fixed by having ONE arm, not two in step: `drivers::block::sdhc_write_veto` (§SDHCPOST at that file's tail) is the definition, both readers forward to it, and it takes the CALLER'S refusal string as a parameter so the knob-off twin is `#[inline(always)] fn(s) -> Some(s)` and `knoboff sdw-rw` measures byte-identity instead of being promised it. **CMD25 IS NOW ROUTED, AND THE NUMBER IS THE REASON.** B140 left `write_blocks_sdhc` on a CMD24 loop because `cmd24 == bytes / 512` was a published prediction — correct, and resting on a premise (“one sector per file-verb write is the common case”) that is FALSE for the workload that asked for the posture: `prtscr` hands `SLICE_WRITE` = 32 KiB per `write_grow`, `write_grow` pushes the whole-sector interior through `write_span` → `fat::write_sectors`, which chunks at `MAX_BLOCKS_PER_OP` = `STORAGE_DATA_BYTES/512` = **64**, and `sdhc::MB_MAX_BLOCKS` is **64** too — so one capture slice is EXACTLY one CMD25, and the rMBP's 15.5 MB screenshot is **~484 multi-block writes where the loop issued ~31,700 single-block ones, ~64x fewer card transactions**, each saved one a command, a response, a Buffer-Write-Ready re-arm and a DAT0 busy poll. The counter is renamed `SECTORS` and the ROUTE IS GATED ON `sdw-rw`, NOT `sdw` — the honest gate rather than the convenient one: a counter's NAME must name the command the card saw, so a `ro` build (whose only FAT-layer writes are 4c's reserved-extent ones, which every capture since 4c is read against) keeps the CMD24 loop and prints `cmd24=` VERBATIM, and only an `sdw-rw` build takes CMD25 and prints `sectors=`, whose prediction `sectors == bytes / 512` is true of both commands and names neither. Neither polarity's witness lies, no existing capture is re-based, and — MEASURED — `knoboff sdw` stays byte-identical, which it could not have done had the rename landed on the shipped line (the first measurement came back `58132 byte(s) differ` for exactly that reason, and the strings diff named the one cause). **WHAT SDHC-4c LOSES, as a RETIREMENT and not an exception.** With the volume rw a file verb IS a FAT mutator, so 4c's “no knob widens the set” and “the card acquires a writer that is not a FAT mutator” stop being true while the knob is on; `fs/sdhc4c.rs` says so in its own module doc rather than leaving them standing, the permit bypass says so on the wire once, and a FAT/directory RMW is accounted as `mutation expected` against its own counter so the `!!` defect line keeps its exact meaning on every `ro` capture. Widening the extent instead cannot work: a capture CREATES a file (directory RMW), GROWS it (an `alloc_cluster` per 32 KiB, each a FAT write to every copy) and publishes its size LAST — metadata below `data_start`, where §11's proof shows the extent can never reach, so a widened extent admits the data and refuses the file. **R54, the third blocker.** PRTSCR's no-session refusal is checked FIRST, ahead of the PRTSCR-VOL ladder (“a capture that can never belong to anyone must not spin up the ladder”), so with no session NO posture lands a capture; arroyo's `UNAOS_LOGIN` note claimed the x86 builder carried no mapping, which was STALE — it maps both `UNAOS_LOGIN` and `UNAOS_LOGINST` — and the note is corrected in place, because a false note in the knob map is how a lane stays believed-impossible. **⚠ THE DECISION, FOR PETER, RESTATED FROM B140 WITH ITS PRICE.** Does the boot volume's DEFAULT posture become `rw`? The card IS this machine's hard drive. **If YES (whole volume rw by default):** the machine behaves like a computer — screenshots, logs, holocron and any future app write where a user expects them, with no second medium to carry away. The price is POWER-CUT EXPOSURE on a filesystem with NO JOURNAL: a cut between the FAT write and the directory write strands a cluster chain nothing points at; a cut between two FAT copies leaves them disagreeing; and there is no fsck in this tree to reconcile either. 4c's reserve-once shape had ZERO exposure to both, because it never touched a FAT or directory sector at all. **If NO (ro with a RESERVED WRITABLE AREA):** the power-cut exposure stays exactly zero and the SDHC-4c permit ladder keeps its job — but the reserved area cannot hold a screenshot, for the structural reason above (the metadata is out of reach of any extent), so captures need either a carry-away USB stick (PRTSCR-VOL rung 2, which the bench does not have) or a host-staged pre-allocated file per capture, which is not a filesystem. **The mechanism built here serves both answers and takes neither: the default is UNCHANGED (`ro`), `rw` is opt-in by `UNAOS_SDW_RW=1`, and flipping the default later is one line in the `sdw-rw` feature's polarity.** ⚠ **PETER ANSWERED IT WHILE THIS ARC WAS IN FLIGHT — R59 (2026-09-22), verbatim “read write.”** The boot volume mounts READ-WRITE BY DEFAULT on every board; ONE CELL PER TAP, NOT PER CORE, and the error is ONE-SIDED BY CONSTRUCTION: a second core's `submit` overwrites the stamp, so the first closer measures from the LATER stamp (short) and the second finds 0 and charges nothing — contention can only SHRINK a reading, never invent one, which is DRAINCAP's own polarity. `tap_sum` and `taps_us` are measured at different seams and do not add up; the remainder is the block, not a tap, and the doc says so. | B162 | **PETER SAW A VUG WHOSE LINES WERE NOT ONE CRYSTAL, AND THE MECHANISM WAS THE RELEASE WORD: `PHASE.store(frame + 1)` DERIVED THE WORKERS' RELEASE EDGE FROM THE PRESENTED-FRAME COUNTER, WHICH VUGTRUTH HAD DELIBERATELY FROZEN ON A FAILED PRESENT.** Flight 11 (2026-09-22), verbatim: *"vug opens struggling so it tries to display the basic line drawing but it turns into abstract art."* Read precisely, that cannot be a second renderer: the crystal is ALWAYS a line drawing (`draw_line` per edge), so "abstract art" is the lit pixels of ONE surface not being ONE wireframe. **THE MECHANISM, `crates/user-vug/src/main.rs` at the `if live > 0` release.** A worker leaves its wait on `p != last` — the release is an EDGE, and an edge needs the value to CHANGE. VUGTRUTH moved `frame += 1` onto the present's SUCCESS branch on purpose, so the fps readout would stop counting frames the eye never received; the unnoticed cost is that a FAILED present freezes `frame` and the next frame republishes the word the workers already hold. No edge, no release. Both workers stay parked (`wake_phase` wakes them; they re-read the same word and park again), `DONE` never reaches `live`, and the parent blocks at the barrier — HAVING ALREADY published the new projection and rasterised its OWN band `BAND_PAR..SH`. **It never presents that frame, and that is why no present-side witness could see this**: the surface is simply LEFT holding rows 0..216 at one rotation and 216..288 at the next, and the compositor composites a live window from the SURFACE on the panel's cadence, not on this program's presents. Holding `frame` still is right for a METER, wrong for a DEADLINE, and wrong for a RELEASE. The cat-own leg compares CONTENT byte-for-byte and the pattern is printable ASCII ON PURPOSE, so `busx_sanitize` is the IDENTITY on it and the compare is honest rather than laundered through a transform; the cp-own leg reads the copy back through the DIRECT path and compares it to the original (`copy_head=0x452d363858535542 orig_head=0x452d363858535542`, 16 B each). **THE WRITE SIDE IS DISTINGUISHED BY CHANNEL, NOT BY NUMBER.** B153 promised write/rm/mv answer `-ENOSYS` in a well-formed reply rather than `-EINVAL`; M3 asserts the sharpest available form of that: a malformed frame (a caller-supplied principal) is refused by `SYS_MSEND` ITSELF with `-EINVAL` and queues NOTHING, while an unfulfilled verb returns 0 from the send and carries `-ENOSYS` in a reply — and the "queued nothing" half is PROVEN, not asserted, by checking that the next reply taken echoes the NEXT request's `corr`. **THE RESULTS CROSS FROM RING 3 AS A SEALED TABLE, AND THE SEAL IS NOT CEREMONY.** The fixture writes both answers per leg into its own window and the launcher reads them while the slot is still live. The window is SCRUBBED TO ZERO at build and `0` is a VALID leg answer (`ok`) — so without a seal written LAST, a fixture that died before its first leg would present nine perfectly-agreeing zeros and read as a PASS. **AND THE FINDING, WHICH IS A CEILING AND WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN REASONED: `NWSTAGE` IS THREE FOR THE WHOLE MACHINE AND `open_created_sibling` DOES NOT SHARE A SLOT — IT ALLOCATES AND SEEDS ITS OWN.** So VERIFYING a bus `cp` costs three writable-staging slots at once: the source, the destination the fulfiller KEPT (`busx_cp`'s honest-scope note), and the sibling that reads the copy back. With `busx86-other` still holding ONE created file open there is no third slot and the read-back is `-EMFILE`: the first green build printed `cp-copy open_rc=-24` and `payload … cp=DIFF` with every equivalence leg already agreeing. This is NOT a bus asymmetry — the direct copy path pays the same — but it is a real property of a bus `cp` on this arch: it is VERIFIABLE ONLY WHEN THE STAGING POOL HAS ROOM. The fixture is therefore two-phase (every leg needing another row's live file first, then the counterparty releases, then the copy is made and checked), and the ceiling retires with the descriptor-free create that retires the honest-scope note itself — STOR-1's line, not the bus's. **A SECOND THING THAT CEILING TAUGHT, AND IT IS THE ONE THAT COULD HAVE LOST DATA SILENTLY.** The U10 deferred-op queue is ONE deep and its overflow is a DROPPED ACKNOWLEDGED MUTATION. So M3's cleanup unlinks ONE file per GO step with the launcher draining between, AND RECORDS EVERY UNLINK'S RC into the verdict (`unlinked=`) — a cleanup step that silently did nothing must never be able to read as a clean one.
